---
title: "Writing a Hook"
---

# Writing Your First Hook

After this page you have a `pre-commit` that refuses a commit containing a tab-only whitespace error, and a `commit-msg` that checks a conventional subject.

## `pre-commit`

```bash
cat > ~/desk/desk-api/.git/hooks/pre-commit <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
git diff --cached --check
EOF
chmod +x ~/desk/desk-api/.git/hooks/pre-commit
```

`git diff --cached --check` flags leftover conflict markers and bad whitespace in the **index**. Exit status non-zero aborts the commit.

Try:

```bash
cd ~/desk/desk-api
printf 'bad \n' >> README.md    # trailing space
git add README.md
git commit -m "docs: trigger hook"
```

Fix the line, `git add`, commit again.

## `commit-msg`

Git passes the path to a temporary file that holds the message:

```bash
cat > ~/desk/desk-api/.git/hooks/commit-msg <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
file="$1"
subject="$(head -n1 "$file")"
if [[ "$subject" == WIP* ]]; then
  echo "commit-msg: subject cannot start with WIP" >&2
  exit 1
fi
EOF
chmod +x ~/desk/desk-api/.git/hooks/commit-msg
```

A stricter conventional check can wait until the team agrees on types. Start by blocking `WIP`.

## `pre-push`

Git passes the remote name and URL, and on stdin: local ref, local hash, remote ref, remote hash.

```bash
cat > ~/desk/desk-api/.git/hooks/pre-push <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
while read -r local_ref local_sha remote_ref remote_sha; do
  if [[ "$remote_ref" == refs/heads/main && "$local_sha" != "$remote_sha" ]]; then
    echo "pre-push: running tests before updating main" >&2
    # python -m pytest -q || exit 1
  fi
done
EOF
chmod +x ~/desk/desk-api/.git/hooks/pre-push
```

Uncomment the test command when `desk-api` has tests.

## `--no-verify`

```bash
git commit --no-verify -m "docs: skip hooks"
```

Emergency only. Treat it as breaking the seatbelt.
